messages:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding Lunaria-7B into staging today. Found a weird clause in their license re: distribution to edge devices. Pasting the snippet below.

maria: ```\n4. Redistribution and Service Hosting. You may provide access to the Model via a hosted API or internal service for evaluation, but you may not distribute the Model weights, checkpoints, or any format that would enable running the Model outside of the Provider’s infrastructure without express written permission.\nAttribution must include the Provider and the original model card.\n``` 

sam: So the question is: does pushing quantized weights to customer-managed devices count as "distribute"? We plan to run 4-bit builds for on-device latency tests.

rachel-legal: Short answer: probably yes — handing over derived weights usually qualifies as redistribution. The clause is pretty explicit: "enable running the Model outside of the Provider’s infrastructure". Even quantized or re-parameterized weights are still a derivative that enables local inference.

anya: For clarity — our Dedicated customers sometimes want a Docker image with the model baked in for air-gapped infra. That would definitely be a distribution, right?

rachel-legal: Yes. Packaging weights inside an image and handing to a customer = distribution. Two paths: (1) get explicit permission from upstream to allow redistributed derivatives (ask for a sublicense or a commercial redistribution addendum), or (2) offer serving-only options (hosted API or a signed runtime container that pulls weights at install time under EULA) — but the latter still needs review.

jin: Implementation note: we can keep experiments internal by running quant tests on our infra and sending benchmark reports to customers. That avoids shipping weights. But for Private deployments where customers manage runtimes, we need a license clearance.

sam: Bench results quick note: 4-bit LLA-4 quant gives ~2.9% relative drop on our conversational evals and 1.8x throughput improvement. Want to continue experiments but not release artifacts.

license-bot: "+1 — suggested mitigation: add model to \"staging:hosted-only\" policy. Tagging infra and policies. See: https://internal.redwood/docs/model-eligibility#hosted-only"

maria: Agreed. I'll set staging to hosted-only and run internal quant bench copies. If legal can get a contact, we can ask for redistribution rights for quantized derivatives.

rachel-legal: I'll draft a short permission request to Lunaria authors. Proposed ask: permission to distribute quantized derivatives under a sublicense that requires attribution and forbids further redistribution. Also request clarification on whether signed runtime containers that pull weights at install-time are permitted.

anya: Can we also request permission to allow customers to run the model in "dedicated" mode (where we manage weights in the VPC but don't hand them over)? That's a common ask.

rachel-legal: Yes — include that. Recommend we propose three tiers in the email: internal evals (allowed), managed dedicated hosting (allowed with attribution + audit log), and full weight redistribution (disallowed unless explicitly granted).

jin: For the meantime, I'll add a config flag so packaging pipeline can produce a non-exportable bundle: `redwood pack --model lunaria-7b --no-export --attach-license meta.json` to prevent accidental export.

sam: Nice. Also let's add a note to the eval PR describing the license constraints so CI doesn't push artifacts to the model registry public bucket.

maria: Will do. Opening a ticket: https://phabricator.redwood/T-4982 (Lunaria onboarding — license clarification + hosted-only staging). I'll @rachel-legal on the ticket.

rachel-legal: Thanks — ping me when the ticket is created. If they respond with a permissive addendum we can re-evaluate distribution for edge customers. Until then, hosted-only and internal quant benches.

maria: Thanks all. Quick checklist to follow: 1) set hosted-only policy, 2) add pack pipeline `--no-export`, 3) run quant benches, 4) legal outreach. I'll update T-4982 with bench results.

anya: (note) I'll attach the current eval script and seed prompts to the ticket so legal can see how we test.

sam: :thumbsup:

maria: Closing the thread here; feel free to DM for anything urgent.
